title: Track the Streak, Not the Score
description: Marking each day you show up is more encouraging — and more honest — than judging how well you did.

body.heading: A cross on the calendar
paragraphs: A simple streak tracker asks only one question: did you show up today? A cross, a tick, a dot in a notebook. It does not grade the quality of the effort, and that is its strength — a rough, tired ten minutes still earns the mark.
Grading yourself every day turns a habit into an exam, and exams create avoidance. Showing up, by contrast, is almost always within your control, even on the worst days.

body.heading: When a day gets missed
paragraphs: Streaks break. Travel, illness and plain forgetfulness happen to everyone. The useful rule is simple: never miss twice in a row if you can help it. One missed day is an event; the second is the start of a new pattern.
If you do miss, restart with the smallest version of the habit the very next day. The streak that matters most is not the longest one — it is the one you are willing to begin again.

takeaway: Count the days you showed up, and forgive the rest.
